newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds mixed, 2007 bond attracts buyers.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds mixed, 2007 bond attracts buyers.

text.p: Danish bond prices were largely unchanged in a cautious market on Tuesday with the focus on the afternoon's U.S. Federal reserve meeting and the forthcoming local seven percent 2007 benchmark.
"Foreign investors are positioning themselves in the forthcoming 2007 benchmark state bond, otherwise the market is wary up to the FOMC meeting," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was unchanged from its opening 110.86, 0.18 point down from Friday's close, yielding 6.35 percent in turnover of 500 million crowns.

The new seven percent 2007 benchmark-to-be traded at 103.38 at 1115 gmt, down 0.52 point from Friday, 0.04 point lower than at the Tuesday opening, yielding 6.53 percent in 3.2 billion crown turnover.

The benchmark yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 73 basis points, while the differential with the 2007 bond was 55 points. The 2006 June future fell 0.56 point to 110.68 with only one contract traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.90 point to 89.10. The crown traded at 3.8082 per mark at 1125 gmt. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33-969652
